reader.requirement: At --std 85, a MERGE with an OUTPUT PROCEDURE must pass control to the procedure during the MERGE, with the merge ready to give the next record in merged order on each RETURN, and when control passes the last statement of the procedure (a paragraph, a section, or a THRU range, with RETURNs possibly in paragraphs PERFORMed from it) the merge must end and control go to the next executable statement after the MERGE - including inside an IF, as the last statement of a PERFORMed paragraph, and when the procedure returns only some records or none.

edition-consulted.switches: Year < 2002 runs GateReleaseReturnRange: a RETURN must lie in the execution range (closure over PERFORM/GO TO) of an output procedure for its file, else COBOL7081 (§1985:XI.4.3.3 SR3); 2002+ leaves it to the run-time EC
Year >= 2023 arms refuse a file SORT/MERGE written in an output procedure; the 85 arm is the edition's own placement rule

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the run-time control transfer (bounded __Dispatch of the procedure range, the merge then CLOSEs and falls through) is the same code at every edition; only the compile-time placement screens of RETURN/MERGE differ
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb3511 covers a THRU range ending at the program's last paragraph reached by GO TO; not exercised: a SECTION output procedure, a RETURN in a paragraph PERFORMed from the range, MERGE inside IF with a following statement, MERGE as the last statement of a PERFORMed paragraph, a procedure that returns one record or none

probes.printed: M1 / OUT-1 / R AAA..R DDD / OUT-3 LAST / AFTER-M1 CNT=4 / FIRST AAA / AFTER-M2 IN-IF / IN-NONE / AFTER-M3 / OUT-1 ... OUT-3 LAST / AFTER-PERFORM-M4 CNT=4 / END (EXPECT: MATCH)
probes.expected: GR9: procedure entered once, each RETURN gives the next merged record, after the procedure's last statement control goes to the statement after the MERGE (same IF branch; back to the PERFORM); partial and zero RETURNs still terminate the merge; USING files closed afterwards (OPEN INPUT succeeds)

probes.expected: refused: the output procedure must name a procedure

probes.expected: §1985:XI.4.1.4 GR8 range includes PERFORMed statements, so the 85-only GateReleaseReturnRange must not refuse it

reader.notes: The output procedure is emitted as a bounded dispatch of its pc range after SortMerge and SortEnterProcedure; the dispatcher's bounded return is the inserted return mechanism, and the statement's finally drops the store. A first probe with DESCENDING keys over ascending files printed FIRST BBB, which is GR6's undefined result for unordered input, not a fault; the corrected probe matches.

refuter.evidence: p1last.cob (refute-1985-034/p1last-001) attacked the return mechanism at 'the end of the last statement in the output procedure'. Inside OUT-1 THRU OUT-3, OUT-1 does PERFORM OUT-3, which is the procedure's last paragraph. Control came back to the PERFORM ('OUT-1 BACK FROM PERFORM OUT-3') and the merge did not end early. The RETURN loop then ran by GO TO OUT-2, OUT-3 ran last, and control passed to 'AFTER-MERGE-1 CNT=3'. Later, ordinary sequential flow with no MERGE active fell through the same paragraphs ('FT OUT-1', ' OUT-3') and went on to TAIL-P ('TAIL REACHED PASS=1'), so the return mechanism is active only during the MERGE. The 85-only GateReleaseReturnRange accepted a RETURN reached by GO TO inside the range. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XI.4.1.4 GR9  (4.1.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR9'.
